text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Boris Yeltsin's younger daughter, Tatyana Dyachenko, promises after being appointed a presidential adviser to remain in the shadows and says she is the best person to tell unpleasant things to the president.
- Andrei Vavilov, president of the International Company for Finance and Investments, failed to win a seat on the board of directors of GAZPROM at the company's latest shareholders meeting.
- Moscow car maker AZLK starts production of the new Moskvich executive model which will cost about $20,000.
- The licence to develop Irkutsk's biggest gold mine, Sykhoi Log, will be handed to the local administration.
- Tyumen oil company, one of the biggest oil producers in Russia, which will auction 40 percent of its shares on July 18, is planning to make personnel changes in its board of directors.
- Russia's government is planning to pay off its arrears to the military in the next month.
- The law on shares production is likely to be approved by Russia's upper house of parliament, the head of parliament's committee on natural resourses says.
- Caspian oil will not be transported via Chechnya if the region's leaders continue insisting on its sovereignty, says a LUKoil official.
- Russia's leading financial groups face a major fight over six oil companies which are about to be auctioned.
- Government supporters are leading after the first round of local elections in Nizhny Novgorod and Samara.
- Alexander Nikitin, a former Soviet officer accused of treason after revealing facts about Russia's nuclear waste dumping activities, is to face new charges, according to his lawers.
